subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config/API shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix intentionally changes authorization semantics between requester agents and spawned children and adds public config surface in a security-sensitive area.

options.title: Sponsor Delegate-Only Config
options.body: Add a documented `selfDeny`/`delegateOnly`-style field with deny precedence, audit/diagnostic behavior, and runtime/ACP semantics covered by tests.

options.title: Fold Into Per-Spawn Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until the per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Reject New Core Surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or behavior-level delegation as the supported pattern and accept that config-enforced separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Delegate-Only Config
recommendation.body: Add a documented `selfDeny`/`delegateOnly`-style field with deny precedence, audit/diagnostic behavior, and runtime/ACP semantics covered by tests.
